subject: Post-call: Devbench config & local run playbook
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Ashley Park <ashley@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Devbench config & local run playbook

Thanks again for taking the time today, Ashley — great sync. Quick recap + pragmatic next steps so we keep momentum on the Pilot (Devbench) scope.

Highlights from the call:
- Goal: validate latency and routing for our reranker + embeddings flow against your anonymized dataset (~50k queries/day).
- Priority integrations: auth (OIDC for service-to-service), model routing policy (latency first, fallback to smaller quantized variant), and tool-calling for structured output from claims extraction.
- Success criteria: P95 < 250ms end-to-end for tiered traffic, consistent embeddings cosine stability within expected tolerances, and a short-lived canary rollout to 10% traffic.

Proposed immediate deliverables (we can iterate):
1) Devbench config playbook (attached) — step-by-step local env + smoke checks for Python + TypeScript samples.
2) Local sample apps (zip attached) — minimal Python FastAPI + TS Node server wiring auth, routing, and embeddings calls.
3) Mutual action plan: kick off 2-week pilot (week A: env setup + auth; week B: reranker/embeddings run + results).

Ask for Lumina: please confirm the test dataset window (anonymized), and share the OIDC issuer URL and a short-lived test client credentials pair we can use in the sandbox. We can also accept temporary API token if you prefer to avoid spinning up client creds.

Next meeting: propose Oct 10, 11am PT for a 30-min setup walkthrough. If that works, Marissa will send a calendar invite with links.

Attachments: devbench-config-playbook.pdf, local-sample-apps.zip

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Ashley Park <ashley@luminahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Hsu <michael.h@luminahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Devbench config & local run playbook

Thanks, Sean — great summary. Quick answers and a couple of clarifications: 

- Dataset: we can provide an anonymized 14-day dump in S3 (CSV + JSONL) — will confirm the exact path by EOD tomorrow.
- Auth: OIDC issuer is https://auth.luminahealth.com/. We can create a client-id/client-secret for the sandbox env; prefer to hand over a short-lived client to Redwood for the pilot.
- Routing: happy with latency-first routing; one ask — can the fallback model preserve top-3 rerank ordering? If quantization changes ordering materially, we need a regression alert.

Questions from our side:
1) How invasive is the local sample app setup? Our infra folks prefer a containerized run that mirrors our staging network.
2) For structured outputs (claims extraction) we may want to optionally call a downstream webhook from the model responses — is that supported in the sample?

Can join Oct 10, 11am PT. Thanks for setting this up.

—Ashley
Director, Data Products | Lumina Health
ashley@luminahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ashley Park <ashley@luminahealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Devbench config & local run playbook

Nice — answering the items and mapping owners below. I also attached the step-by-step playbook in PDF and included a small ZIP of sample apps (Node + Python) that spin up locally in Docker.

1) Local setup invasiveness: low. The samples are containerized and use docker-compose to mimic a minimal staging network:
   - python-sample: FastAPI app that performs auth (OIDC client credentials), hits Redwood hosted endpoint, and writes embeddings to a local vector store (we include a memory-backed stub).
   - ts-sample: Express server that demonstrates function/tool calling for structured output and an example reranker call.

2) Webhook support: yes. The TS sample includes an optional webhook consumer (local URL configured via env) and a short guide for secure verification (HMAC header).

Action items + owners:
- Marissa: Send calendar invite for Oct 10, 11am PT + provide access to drive folder (today).
- Ashley: Share test dataset S3 path + confirm client-credential approach (by Oct 4 EOD).
- Grace: Prepare baseline eval prompt set (20 queries) to validate ranking/regression checks during the canary.
- Sean: Run initial smoke run locally, capture latency profile, and share results in the Drive link.

Attachments: devbench-config-playbook.pdf, local-sample-apps.zip

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Ashley Park <ashley@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Devbench config & local run playbook

Perfect — sending invite now. I'll start the local smoke run against the samples this morning and drop an initial latency snapshot in the Drive folder (link in the playbook). If you post the S3 path I'll wire up a tiny ingestion script to pull the anonymized set into the local vector stub so we can run the reranker flow end-to-end.

See you on Oct 10.

—Sean
